[F1] **Paths, measurability and local boundedness.** After the statement's $\mathcal F_0$-null-event normalization, $X$ is adapted with everywhere continuous paths, hence predictable, and on each finite time interval a continuous path is bounded. Every continuous function of $(s,X_s)$ is predictable; its product with the predictable coefficient $\sigma$ is predictable, while its product with the progressively measurable drift $b$ is progressively measurable. [F7] **Localization of the class and of the coefficients.** For $c>0$ put $D_c:=\{|X_0|\le c\}\in\mathcal F_0$ and $\rho_c:=\inf\{t:\max(|X_t|,\int_0^t|b|,\int_0^t\sigma^2)\ge c\}\wedge T$. Then $\rho_c$ is a stopping time: for $t<T$, the event $\{\rho_c\le t\}$ is the event that the running supremum of the continuous adapted process $\max(|X|,\int|b|,\int\sigma^2)$ on $[0,t]$ is at least $c$. This supremum is the supremum over rational times together with $t$, hence is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable; for $t\ge T$ the stopping event is the whole space. The process $\bar X^{(c)}:=1_{D_c}X^{\rho_c}$ is a continuous Brownian Ito process with initial value $1_{D_c}X_0$ and coefficients $1_{D_c}b1_{[0,\rho_c]}$, $1_{D_c}\sigma1_{[0,\rho_c]}$. It is bounded by $c$, its drift variation and diffusion energy on $[0,T]$ are at most $c$, and on $D_c\cap\{\rho_c\ge T\}$ it and all its integrals coincide with those of $X$. These events increase to a probability-one event as $c\to\infty$, because $X$ is continuous and $\int|b|,\int\sigma^2$ are finite and continuous in the upper limit almost surely.
